name: dual-sink-watcher
description: Read one page and land it in BOTH durable places at once: a queryable knowledge item you can search, and a stable artifact you can open, link and version. One fetch, two sinks, one grounding check between them. The host must be on your egress allow-list first.

url.help: The page to read. Its host must already be listed under Settings → Security → Allowed Egress Hosts — automated fetches use an EXCLUSIVE allow-list, so an unlisted host is refused before any request leaves the machine.

subject.help: What this page is about, in your words. It is the knowledge item's identity, so re-reading the page updates one record instead of creating a second.

artifact_slug.help: The artifact to keep current — lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, because it becomes a directory name. An unknown slug is created on the first run and updated on every one after.

max_chars.help: How much of the page to read. This can only NARROW the fetch provider's 20,000-character ceiling — a bigger number gets you the ceiling, never more.

metadata.why_cheap: One standard-tier read of the page plus one grounding judge. Both sinks are zero-token actions on content the engine has already resolved, and they run concurrently — writing twice costs nothing extra in model calls.
metadata.which_two_sinks_and_why: `knowledge-persist` and `artifact-update` — the platform's two DURABLE writes, chosen because they have different READ paths. The knowledge store answers "what do we know about this" through retrieval and dedupes on logical identity; the artifact registry gives one stable slug a person opens, links, embeds and versions on `snapshot`. `notify` is deliberately NOT the second sink: a dashboard ping is transient, so a template that delivered there and nowhere else would have nothing left to show tomorrow.
metadata.egress_is_the_consent_surface: `net-fetch` reaches nothing until this page's host sits in `security.egress.allow_hosts`. With an empty list the first run FAILS by design, naming the host and the exact setting — that refusal is how the user grants the reach, and this template has no way to widen it.
metadata.the_cadence_is_the_triggers_not_a_loops: "Watcher" here means the shape, not an in-run loop: the graph is one pass, and repetition comes from the schedule or event trigger you attach to it. A run that held itself open for a day would occupy a lane and die with the process, where a trigger survives a restart.

steering_examples.description: Keep reading our dependency's changelog page into knowledge and into the changelog artifact so I can open the latest version any time.
The artifact is accumulating a version per run and burying the ones I care about — stop snapshotting and just overwrite it.

example_outputs: one searchable knowledge item and one openable artifact, both current with the page and both citing it
metadata.when_not_to_use: not when you only want to hear about CHANGES — that is market-monitor, which stays quiet unless something material moved
